sub_scenario.family: negotiating scope commitments when project evidence is incomplete
sub_scenario.one_line: university laboratory coordinator: grant a conditional trial rather than recurring access

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the equipment register and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The methods folder review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can reserve a microscope for a class when its protocol and consumables list are approved.
Is sharing equipment generally difficult?
No, when the method has been reviewed and the booking has a clear boundary.
Someone new shadowed me in the laboratory office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the teaching terms into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The materials group has requested recurring access to the imaging suite, but supplied only a one-page aim and no sample handling procedure.
What would recurring access assume?
That their samples are compatible, staff time exists, and the equipment can be cleaned safely.
I previously hosted a visiting group for a one-day trial using our established sample process.
Why did that work?
Their samples matched the existing protocol and a technician was assigned.
I archived last cycle's notes on the methods folder and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The suite has one unused afternoon each fortnight and a technician can support a supervised trial.
Does that create a standing arrangement?
No, it creates a controlled opportunity to learn what their method requires.
A vendor call about the equipment register ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the laboratory office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the teaching terms.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the methods folder records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The group has agreed to submit sample details in advance and use the supervised trial to produce a handling procedure before requesting further slots.
What can you reasonably grant?
One supervised trial, with later access depending on the resulting procedure.
I sketched next week's plan for the teaching terms before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the equipment register updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The next teaching term begins in seven weeks.
Why is that relevant?
Any recurring use must be understood before it competes with teaching bookings.
I compared two options for the methods folder tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the laboratory office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Can I offer the materials group recurring use of the imaging suite?

replacement_dialogue.content: I filed the routine teaching terms paperwork and confirmed the owner list.
I did a standard pass over the methods folder records this morning.
The group has agreed to a supervised trial but says it will bring samples without advance details and decide the procedure afterward.
Would that support the same grant?
No, the trial would no longer control the key uncertainty.
